name: TerraScope
description: A reproducible benchmark measuring what land-cover classification accuracy is achievable on CPU-only hardware, and what each accuracy point costs in energy. Five ImageNet-pretrained architectures (ResNet-50, MobileNetV3-Small/Large, EfficientNet-Lite0, MobileViT-S) are trained on EuroSAT under one identical recipe across five seeds each, exported to ONNX at fp32 and int8 (dynamic and static), and measured through ONNX Runtime's CPU execution provider for accuracy, latency, memory and energy. Finding: EfficientNet-Lite0 quantised to int8-static reaches 97.45% (95% CI +/- 0.32) at 3.18 J per 1,000 inferences, against ResNet-50 fp32's 98.12% (+/- 0.30) at 60.84 J -- 19x the energy for 0.67 percentage points. Accuracy differences between architectures are real (8 of 10 pairwise comparisons survive Holm-Bonferroni correction) but span only 1.25pp, while energy spans a factor of 19. On CPU-only hardware the deployment decision therefore belongs to energy and latency, not accuracy. Self-audited. The benchmark measures its own assumptions rather than only declaring them. The committed ONNX graphs are re-timed on x86 Linux in CI and rank agreement with the Apple M2 is reported (Spearman rho ~0.68), so the ordering is presented as an Apple Silicon ordering rather than assumed portable. The CPU package's share of on-die power is measured at 99.80% across 89,983 samples, bounding what the energy figures exclude and independently confirming the matrix ran on the CPU.
